description: Five-panel composite EBSD figure of the TD sample deformed to 15% engineering strain. (a) Phase + band-slope (BS) map with a 20 µm scale bar, overlaying FCC phase (green) on BCC phase + BS (red), with a BS colour bar at right running from 20 to 255; a bordered field is labelled "γ+α+α′" and δ grains are marked; loading geometry is drawn as RD up and TD//LD to the right. (b) Frequency (%) versus Band Slope plot (x ≈ 30–255, y = 0.000–0.010) with the experimental distribution (grey circles) deconvoluted into Martensite (blue) and Ferrite (red) components; the blue α′-martensite peak lies near the 100 band-slope gridline and the red ferrite peak between the 150 and 200 gridlines, and a black arrow marks the cut-off at the intersection of the two peaks. (c) KAM map of the same field, 20 µm scale bar, 0–3° colour bar, dominated by low-misorientation blue with green bands. (d) Magnified Phase + BS map, 3 µm scale bar, legend γ (green, FCC), α/δ (red, BCC), α′ (grey, martensite); black arrows show α′-martensite nucleating at austenite/ferrite boundaries. (e) KAM map of the FCC phase only within (d), 3 µm scale bar, 0–3°; red arrows mark high-KAM bands at α′/γ heterointerfaces. The group argues that strain-induced α′-martensite nucleates preferentially at phase boundaries where GND density is highest.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a phase + band-slope EBSD map with a 20 µm scale bar, using green for FCC phase and red for BCC phase with BS shading, and a BS colour bar spanning 20 to 255.
Panel (a) labels a region as 'γ+α+α′' and annotates individual δ grains, with a coordinate legend indicating RD vertical and TD//LD horizontal.

Panel (b) plots Frequency (%) against Band Slope (x-axis approximately 30–255, y-axis 0.000–0.010) and contains three series: Experiment (grey open circles), Martensite (blue open circles) and Ferrite (red open circles).

In panel (b) the martensite component peaks at a lower band slope (near the 100 gridline) than the ferrite component (between the 150 and 200 gridlines), producing a bimodal overall distribution; a black arrow marks the chosen cut-off point between the two peaks.

Panel (c) is a KAM map of the same field as (a) with a 20 µm scale bar and a 0°–3° colour bar, showing predominantly low (blue) misorientation with a green higher-KAM skeleton; the magnified region of (d)/(e) is marked by a dashed box.

Panel (d) is a magnified Phase + BS map with a 3 µm scale bar whose legend assigns green to γ (FCC), red to α/δ (BCC) and grey to α′ (martensite), and black arrows mark α′-martensite at austenite/ferrite boundaries.
Panel (e) is a KAM (FCC) map of the region in (d) with a 3 µm scale bar and a 0°–3° colour bar, with red arrows pointing to high-misorientation bands located along the α′/γ interfaces.
The caption states that panel (a) is a 'Phase + BS map' covering both α′-martensite, δ/α-ferrite and austenite, and that (b) shows the distribution of BS values for BCC.

The citing text states that the BCC phase exhibits a large variation in band-slope (BS) values and that regions with low BS indicate deformation-induced α′-martensite because of its much higher dislocation density and lattice distortion compared with ferrite.

The citing text states that the bimodal BS distribution of the BCC phase was obtained with AZtecCrystal software and that a BS cut-off at the intersection of the two peaks was used to visualise ferrite and α′-martensite separately.
The citing text states that the UFG γ+α region has a higher KAM value than the δ-ferrite because of the strain-induced α′-martensitic transformation.

The citing text states that α′-martensite nucleation takes place primarily at the phase boundary between austenite and ferrite (α-ferrite or δ-ferrite), as marked by the arrows in panel (d), driven by stress/strain concentration at the heterointerfaces.

The citing text states that higher misorientation values, and therefore a higher geometrically necessary dislocation density, occur at the martensite nucleation sites, as revealed by the KAM map in panel (e).
The citing text states that a similar finding is observed for the RD sample, which is not shown in this figure.

subfigures.description: Phase + BS EBSD map, 20 µm scale bar, showing green FCC grains and red BCC regions whose shade encodes band slope on a 20–255 colour bar; a dashed box labels the UFG 'γ+α+α′' aggregate, isolated δ grains are annotated, and the RD (up) / TD//LD (right) loading geometry is indicated.

Frequency (%) vs Band Slope plot with three series (grey circles = Experiment, blue = Martensite, red = Ferrite); bimodal with the martensite component peaking at lower band slope and ferrite at higher band slope, and a black arrow marking the cut-off at the intersection of the two fitted peaks.
KAM map of the field in (a), 20 µm scale bar, colour bar 0–3°; the map is largely blue (low misorientation) with green, higher-KAM network regions, and a dashed box marks the area magnified in (d).

Magnified Phase + BS map, 3 µm scale bar, with legend γ = green (FCC), α/δ = red (BCC), α′ = grey (martensite); black arrows point to α′-martensite formed along austenite/ferrite phase boundaries, with a large δ grain at right.

KAM map restricted to the FCC phase of the region in (d), 3 µm scale bar, 0–3° colour bar; seven red arrows highlight high-misorientation bands located at the α′/γ interfaces, corresponding to locally elevated GND density.
